title: OpenGHM model input metadata
description: metadata.json for one published model input (ADR 0015) — the ancillary/reference data a WBM run reads besides its climate forcing and network. Grouped the same way the snapshot spec is: about (a person, at publish), coverage and datasets (derived from the input's own data_init/ records), networks (the river-network files it carries). See docs/reference/metadata-format.md.

$schema.description: This document's own schema version URL, e.g. https://schemas.openghm.org/model-input-spec/metadata/1.0.0.json.

id.description: Minted at publish, same rule as a snapshot's id (ADR 0014): 256 random bits as lowercase hex, not derived from content. Two snapshots built from the same input data cite this same value in their uses.modelInput.id.

slug.description: The human name at publish time. Not part of the S3 key; a catalog maps slug to id for browsing, same rule as a snapshot's slug.

coverage.description: The extent of the input as a whole — the union of what its networks and datasets cover. temporalCoverage is optional because a model input can be a static/climatological reference (soil properties, crop coefficients) with no real calendar period at all; when every dataset the input carries is climatological, there is nothing true to put here.

networks.description: River-network / grid-definition files this input carries under network/ — what a snapshot's simulation.spatialCoverage and resolution are actually computed from when its Network key points into a linked model input rather than a bundled copy.

file.description: Path relative to this input's root, e.g. network/hyd_5m_CONUS_mississippi_patched.asc.

datasets.description: One entry per MT record under data_init/ — the reference/ancillary time series and static fields a WBM run reads besides climate forcing (crop calendars, glacier area, irrigation efficiency, soil capacity, ...). `code` is unique within the array; JSON Schema cannot express that, so the generator and the validator enforce it, the same limitation as inputVariables[].role in the snapshot spec. Not every file under data_init/ is an MT record in this shape — one observed in the staged ancillary data (a point-feature reference table with its own DOI and no Code_Name at all) does not fit here and is not modelled by 1.0.0; see open-items.md.

code.description: The record's own Code_Name field. Not assumed from its filename — several records in the staged ancillary data declare a Code_Name that differs from their file's basename.

init.description: Path relative to this input's root, e.g. data_init/climate/merra2_prectotcorr_d.init. Resolves to <model-input>/data_init/<...>.

name.description: The record's Name field. Optional: present on ordinary MT records, but not guaranteed on every shape this array may need to describe in future.

unit.description: The record's Units field, same rule as a snapshot's inputVariables[].unit — not Orig_Units. Optional and, deliberately, never an empty string: several staged records (crop coefficients, added-water fractions) declare Units as the empty string because the quantity is dimensionless, and an absent field says that more plainly than a quoted nothing.

timeSeries.description: The record's Time_Series field, e.g. daily, monthly, yearly, daily_clim, yearly_clim — a _clim suffix marks a climatology (a repeating annual cycle, not a dated series). Free text, not an enum: the staged data already uses more values than the snapshot spec's forcing-role table anticipated, and this array describes ancillary data in general, not only forcing.

temporalCoverage.description: Omitted for a climatological record: the staged data marks 'no real date' with a 0000 placeholder year, which is not a valid date and is not carried here rather than being transcribed.

project.description: The record's Project field. Present on the climate forcing records (e.g. MERRA2); most other ancillary records in the staged data do not carry one.

metadataLink.description: The record's MetadataLink field, when it has one.

citation.description: The record's citation field, kept as the free string it already is rather than parsed into a structured reference — some carry a DOI inline as text, most carry none at all.
